# Sector Command Guidelines
You have been vetted, and approved by the Auroran Colonial Commissions Office. Now, you are able to serve in the capacity of a Colonial Command Field Officer (CCFO), be that a Station Representative, Director of Care or Commissioner. You are the highest of authorities in the sector when serving in these positions, second only to Terrestrial Command Officers. You must act as an example for the rest of the community.
\n
- Command roles (e.g. Station Rep, Commissioner) are held to a high standard of roleplay, and will have instances of LRP behavior scrutinized more heavily.
- Command staff may never embezzle department funds, or they will face fines and a roleban.
- Command is expected to enforce docking laws and collect any fines related to dock loitering.
\n
[bold]If you must end your shift early, check the following list:[/bold]
- Have your ID on your character
- Ensure no role specific equipment (Door remotes, uplinks) is left out, or otherwise not on your person.
- make a call on command radio to announce your departure
- Return to cryosleep.
- if you run into an issue with any of these, ahelp!
\n
[bold]CCFO's may not tax, lease, rent or otherwise impede the use of station resources. This includes:[/bold]
- Charging docking fees, or charging for docking extensions.
- Restricting Vendor Access (e.g. moving machines behind locked doors) without extenuating circumstance
- Restricting access to station resources.
\n
[bold]The Commissioner is to ensure that any recruited rookies receive proper training and are supervised properly at all times.[/bold]
- Rookies should be studying under and working alongside the Commissioner or a designated Lieutenant who can oversee their training as an officer and in Space Law, SOP and server rules relating to the SLE.
- Rookies who refuse training, try to farm playtime or insist on working alone are to be reported in ahelp.
- Repeated incidents with training rookies may be considered a sign of poor leadership, and result in inspection and review of the Commissioner at fault.
